zh.title: 美國FAA投資4.81億美元補助191處機場改善基礎設施
zh.summary: 美國FAA投入4.81億美元補助，升級全美36州與兩領地共191處機場設施。
body: 美國運輸部長 Sean P. Duffy 宣布，聯邦航空管理局（FAA）將透過「機場基礎設施補助計畫」（Airport Infrastructure Grants, AIG）投入 4.81 億美元，用於改善全美各地機場的基礎設施並提升整體安全表現。該項資金發放時間適逢美國勞動節長假旅行高峰前夕，旨在協助機場因應日益增長的旅客需求。
根據 FAA 發布的資訊，本次補助共劃分為 191 筆款項，涵蓋美國 36 個州以及 2 個海外領地的機場。補助資金可用於機場規劃、開發、航廈改善、行李系統升級、跑道與滑行道翻修、道路與聯外交通改善，以及其他與航空安全相關的基礎設施需求。
在個別機場獲得的資助項目中，喬治亞州亞特蘭大哈茨菲爾德-傑克遜國際機場獲撥最高額度的 1 億美元資金，用於跑道、滑行道與航廈的重建工程，以及跑道安全區域的改善計畫。此外，肯塔基州路易斯維爾穆罕默德·阿里國際機場獲得 3,250 萬美元以重建航廈，加州聖地牙哥國際機場（SAN）則獲撥 3,030 萬美元用於航廈建設。
其他獲得重點補助的設施還包括：威斯康辛州密爾瓦基米切爾國際機場獲頒 1,420 萬美元，用於滑行道建設與翻修；德州埃爾帕索國際機場獲得 870 萬美元，用於停機坪翻修工程。另外，威斯康辛州的通用航空機場共計獲得 250 萬美元補助，用於航廈重建、跑道與滑行道翻修以及除雪設備建築的重建工程。
美國運輸部長 Sean P. Duffy 表示，這項關鍵基礎設施投資將為美國家庭提供更順暢與高效的出行體驗，升級跑道基礎設施則是推動交通發展的一部分。FAA 署長 Bryan Bedford 則指出，這些補助金將協助全美各地機場維持安全與高效運作，並滿足現代旅客的需求與未來的挑戰。

en.title: FAA Awards $481 Million in Airport Infrastructure Grants Across US
en.summary: The US FAA is providing $481 million in grants across 36 states and two territories for 191 airport projects.
body: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy has announced that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is investing $481 million to upgrade infrastructure and enhance safety at airports across the United States. The funding release comes ahead of the busy Labor Day travel period, targeting infrastructure improvements across American airports.

The total allocation delivers 191 individual grants to airports located across 36 states and two territories through the Airport Infrastructure Grants (AIG) program. Under program parameters, AIG funding can be utilized for airport planning, development, terminal improvements, baggage system upgrades, runway and taxiway rehabilitation, roadway and access improvements, and other safety-related infrastructure needs.

Key individual awards include $100 million designated for Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) in Georgia to support runway, taxiway, and terminal reconstruction as well as runway safety area improvements. Additionally, Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport (SDF) in Kentucky receives $32.5 million to reconstruct its terminal, while San Diego International Airport (SAN) in California is awarded $30.3 million for terminal construction.

Specific grants also include $14.2 million for Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport in Wisconsin for taxiway construction and rehabilitation, alongside $8.7 million for El Paso International Airport (ELP) in Texas to rehabilitate its apron. Furthermore, general aviation airports in Wisconsin receive a combined $2.5 million for terminal reconstruction, runway and taxiway rehabilitation, and snow-removal-equipment building reconstruction.

Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy noted that investing in critical infrastructure aims to deliver a more seamless and efficient travel experience for American families, describing runway upgrades as an essential component of transportation development. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford highlighted that these infrastructure investments maintain passenger safety and operational efficiency, helping airports fulfill present travel demands while preparing for future operational requirements.

zh.title: REGENT Viceroy Seaglider完成首次載人飛行
zh.summary: REGENT Viceroy原型完成首次載人飛行；兩名乘員；計畫載客12人
body: 美國航太新創公司REGENT Craft宣稱，其Viceroy Seaglider原型已於9月2日在羅德島州納拉甘西特灣上空完成全球首次載人飛行，據稱是至今最大型、全電動的地面效應（WIG）飛行器載人飛行。
該公司表示，本次短暫飛行由兩名組員操作，原型機在約30秒內飛越約1,956英尺（596公尺），高度約33英尺（10公尺）。
REGENT表示，此次載人測試進入新的階段，並正朝向生產12人座交通工具的目標邁進。生產型Viceroy預計可搭載12名乘客與2名組員，最高速度180mph，航程最遠180英里。
報導同時指出，該公司已獲得最大60架Viceroy的訂單承諾，並公布一項與美國海軍陸戰隊作戰實驗室的1,500萬美元合約，惟詳細內容未明。

en.title: REGENT Viceroy Seaglider completes first crewed prototype flight over Narragansett Bay
en.summary: REGENT Viceroy prototype makes first crewed WIG flight; two crew; planned 12-passenger production
body: US aerospace startup REGENT Craft says its Viceroy Seaglider prototype operated what it described as the world's first flight of the largest-ever all-electric wing-in-ground-effect (WIG) craft to fly with people on board.

The company said the brief flight took place on 2 September over Narragansett Bay in Rhode Island, where REGENT is headquartered, with the prototype covering 1,956 ft (596 m) in approximately 30 seconds at an altitude of about 33 ft (10 m).
REGENT said the test moves the Viceroy programme into a new phase of sea trials as it works toward production of a 12-passenger vehicle.
The production Viceroy is planned to carry 12 passengers and two crew members, with a maximum speed of 180 mph and range of up to 180 miles, according to the company.
